forbids: a board artifact that does not say it is not legal advice, and banned vocabulary in any shipped source file — scripts included
note: Enrolled in v0.60.0. Guard-shaped since it was written and classified `candidate` by BL-101's registry, which is how it became countable. BL-121 was the blocker: 51 checks across these nine suites read a crashed probe as a pass, so a mutation registered here would have been registered against a check that could not fail. That closed in v0.59.0.

mutations.why: Drop the `Not legal advice` footer from the board view. It is one list comprehension away at all times, it reads as tidying, and the artifact that loses it is the one a director forwards to counsel. This suite does not scan renderer SOURCE for vocabulary, so the source-scan mutation the other six use passes here — the anchor had to be found against what this suite actually checks rather than assumed from its siblings.
defeats: the board view says it is not legal advice

mutations.why: A file in `scripts/` the guard has never been told about, carrying the vocabulary it forbids. TWO properties at once, and only the `create` form can express either. First, GP-1.7: the scan must read this because the tree has it, not because a list names it. Second, and specific to BL-221: until v0.77.0 this suite globbed `renderers/render_*.py` plus `renderers/_common.py`, so NO edit anywhere in `scripts/` could fail it — the engine that writes most of the strings the renderers print was outside the population entirely. A new file in `scripts/` is the only mutation that tells a scan reading the tree apart from a scan reading a glob that happens to cover the files somebody remembered.
defeats: no banned vocabulary in the executable source of any shipped file
